81.text: The Book of Intellect, Knowledge and Ignorance
Chapter 1: The merit of the intellect and the censure of ignorance

al-Baqara: "signs for a people who use their intellect"; and He, exalted, said: "thus does God make clear to you His signs, that perhaps you may understand"; and He, exalted, said: "yet none takes heed save those possessed of understanding."

Al 'Imran: "yet none takes heed save those possessed of understanding"; and He, exalted, said: "We have made clear to you the signs, if you would use your intellect"; and He said: "truly in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day, there are signs for those possessed of understanding."

al-Ma'ida: "that is because they are a people who do not use their intellect"; and He, exalted, said: "so fear God, O you possessed of understanding"; and He said: "and most of them do not use their intellect."
al-An'am: "but most of them are ignorant"; and He said: "and surely the abode of the hereafter is better for those who are godfearing — will you not then use your intellect?"
al-Anfal: "truly the worst of creatures in God's sight are the deaf and dumb who do not use their intellect."
Yunus: "can you then make the deaf hear, though they do not use their intellect?"; and He, exalted, said: "and He lays defilement upon those who do not use their intellect."
Hud: "but I see you are a people who are ignorant."
Yusuf: "truly We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, that perhaps you may understand."
al-Ra'd: "only those possessed of understanding take heed."
Ibrahim: "and that those possessed of understanding may take heed."
Ta Ha: "truly in that are signs for those possessed of reason."
al-Nur: "thus does God make clear to you the signs, that perhaps you may understand."
al-Zumar: "truly in that is a reminder for those possessed of understanding."

82.text: al-Mu'min: "a guidance and a reminder for those possessed of understanding"; and He, exalted, said: "and that perhaps you may understand."
al-Jathiya: "signs for a people who use their intellect."
al-Hujurat: "most of them do not use their intellect."
al-Hadid: "We have made clear to you the signs, that perhaps you may understand."
al-Hashr: "that is because they are a people who do not use their intellect."

«1»- Ma'ani al-Akhbar; al-Amali of al-Saduq: al-Hafiz, from Ahmad b. 'Abd Allah al-Thaqafi, from 'Isa b. Muhammad al-Katib, from al-Mada'ini, from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, peace be upon him, who said: 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon them both, said: The intellects of women lie in their beauty, and the beauty of men lies in their intellects. (1)

Exposition: al-jamal (beauty) is excellence in form and in character. As for his saying, peace be upon him, "the intellects of women lie in their beauty" — the meaning may be that one ought not to look to their intellect, given its rarity, but rather be content with their beauty; or the meaning may be that their intellect is for the most part bound up with their beauty. The first is the more evident.

«2»- al-Amali of al-Saduq: al-'Attar, from his father, from Sahl, from Muhammad b. 'Isa, from al-Bazanti, from Jamil, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, used to say: The root of a man is his understanding, his intellect is his religion, and his manliness is where he places himself. The days are turns of fortune, and people are equal in their descent from Adam.

Exposition: al-lubb, with a damma on the lam, is the pure essence of anything, and also the intellect; the second is what is meant here. That is, the precedence of individual men in the nobility of their origin rests upon their intellects, not upon their lineages or their ancestral merits. Then he, peace be upon him, explained that the intellect which is the source of nobility appears only through choosing the true religion from among the religions, and through perfecting one's religion with the things that perfect faith. And al-muruwwa, with hamza and with a damma on the mim and the ra', is humanity (2), derived from al-mar' (man); it is sometimes lightened by substitution and assimilation.
